task: OpenClaw owner-gated Mac GUI screen inspection fail-fast
problem: The owner request '지금 떠 있는 쿠팡 화면에 어떤 것들이 보여?' timed out because OpenClaw routed screen reading through raw Peekaboo shell commands. The OpenClaw GUI bridge socket was missing and the local Peekaboo runtime lacked Screen Recording/Accessibility permissions, so three Peekaboo shell calls waited until the user interrupted them after about 122 seconds.

implementation.summary: Added owner-gated harness_screen_inspect routing, one-shot execution-token binding, direct-call rejection, Peekaboo shell blocking during routed screen-inspection turns, bounded fail-fast Peekaboo bridge/permission/screen checks, hardened bridge selection across OpenClaw and Peekaboo sockets, structured follow-up routing for '다시 확인해' after a prior harness_screen_inspect tool call/result, a parsed trajectory fallback for OpenClaw routes that omit historical messages in before_prompt_build, and a Chrome window-id/cg fallback when Peekaboo screen/analyze mode fails.
Documented the native inspect-only screen route and explicit bridge/permission blocker reporting.

Added regression coverage for screen-inspection intent detection, quoted-context isolation, owner/non-owner routing, direct-call rejection, Peekaboo shell blocking, one-shot tool-call binding, duplicate toolCallId idempotence, fail-closed follow-up routing when prior context is only user-controlled text, trajectory fallback that parses structured tool.call/tool.result events instead of trusting quoted text, and largest on-screen Peekaboo window selection.
